examples.problem_statement: Multiply 89 × 117 using the Nikhilam base method

solution.operation: Choose the base 100
solution.description: Both numbers are near this power of 10, so Nikhilam applies

solution.operation: Write the deviations from the base
solution.description: Deviation = number − base

solution.operation: Cross-add for the left part
solution.description: Either cross-sum gives the same left part

solution.operation: Multiply the deviations for the right part
solution.description: The right part occupies 2 digits — the width of the base's zeros

solution.operation: Complete the negative right part from the base
solution.result: \text{the product } -187 \text{ is negative, so complete it from the base: }\;\lceil 187 \div 100 \rceil = 2 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{left } 106 - 2 = 104,\; \text{right } 2\times100 -187 = 13
solution.description: A negative right part is completed from the base — of any width, not only when it is too wide — and the borrowed multiple of the base is subtracted from the left part.

solution.operation: Assemble the answer
solution.description: left \times 100 + right, with the digits placed by width

common_mistakes: sign error when one deviation is positive and the other negative
forgetting to complete a negative right part from the base, and to reduce the left part by the amount borrowed

solution.description: Both numbers are near this power of 10, so Nikhilam applies

solution.operation: Write the deviations from the base
solution.description: Deviation = number − base

solution.operation: Cross-add for the left part
solution.description: Either cross-sum gives the same left part

solution.operation: Multiply the deviations for the right part
solution.description: The right part occupies 3 digits — the width of the base's zeros

solution.operation: Carry the surplus from the right part into the left part
solution.description: The right part may hold only as many digits as the base has zeros; the surplus above that is carried into the left part.

solution.operation: Assemble the answer
solution.description: left \times 1000 + right, with the digits placed by width

common_mistakes: treating the product of two negative deviations as negative, when two minuses give a positive right part
writing the whole product in the right part instead of carrying the overflow into the left part

examples.problem_statement: Multiply 1189 × 946 using the Nikhilam base method

solution.operation: Choose the base 1000
solution.description: Both numbers are near this power of 10, so Nikhilam applies

solution.operation: Write the deviations from the base
solution.description: Deviation = number − base

solution.operation: Cross-add for the left part
solution.description: Either cross-sum gives the same left part

solution.operation: Multiply the deviations for the right part
solution.description: The right part occupies 3 digits — the width of the base's zeros

solution.operation: Complete the negative right part from the base
solution.result: \text{the product } -10206 \text{ is negative, so complete it from the base: }\;\lceil 10206 \div 1000 \rceil = 11 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{left } 1135 - 11 = 1124,\; \text{right } 11\times1000 -10206 = 794

solution.operation: Assemble the answer
solution.description: left \times 1000 + right, with the digits placed by width

common_mistakes: sign error when one deviation is positive and the other negative
forgetting to complete a negative right part from the base, and to reduce the left part by the amount borrowed
